subject.title: Add an "Approve and Run" action for assistant-suggested terminal commands in the Control UI

question: Should Control UI support running assistant-proposed commands, and if so must it use a structured proposal-to-exec-approval contract rather than inferring runnable commands from markdown code blocks?
rationale: This would create a new path from assistant-authored text to local command execution, so the durable command/cwd/host/session binding, risk labels, authorization scopes, and output routing are product and security boundary choices.

options.title: Use structured command proposals
options.body: Add a typed command-proposal contract that creates existing exec approval requests with exact command, cwd, host, session, risk metadata, and result routing before the UI can approve execution.

options.title: Copy-only for now
options.body: Keep assistant shell snippets copy-only and treat this as future operator-console work until maintainers are ready to define the security contract.

options.title: Unify with broader approvals dashboard
options.body: Fold this into a larger approvals/dashboard project with the related pending-approvals and shell-block rendering issues, accepting a larger product scope.

recommendation.title: Use structured command proposals
recommendation.body: Add a typed command-proposal contract that creates existing exec approval requests with exact command, cwd, host, session, risk metadata, and result routing before the UI can approve execution.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the original gateway-routed exec approval surface that this feature would need to extend safely.
